lines.text: There are only four ways to get rid of a kid's wart, ranked from weakest to strongest. Most families never make it to number four.
One wart turned into fifteen. So here's every fix we tried, ranked from weakest to strongest.
Only number four got the root.
R.I.P., my kid's wart. You will not be missed. Here's every fix we tried, ranked from weakest to strongest.
lines.tts: R. I. P., my kid's wart. You will not be missed. Here's every fix we tried, ranked from weakest to strongest.

lines.text: Number one, duct tape. It sits on top of the wart for weeks.
Rent free. It never gets under the hard skin.
Number two, acid pads. A bit stronger.
They peel it down till the black dots are gone. And it always seems to come back.
Number three, freezing at the doctor's. The strongest one most of us know.
Somebody held him still every time.
It was agonizing for all of us.
And after every visit, there were two or three more.
Here's what nobody told me.
Freezing, acid and shaving only snap off the top, like picking a dandelion. The root stays under the hard skin, so it grows back.
Every fix made it look done, but the root never left. It was never our fault.
Number four gets the root. It's RootOut, an oil with four plants, and each one takes it a little deeper.

Lemon goes first and softens the hard top. Tea tree is a thin oil, so it sinks right in, up to 8x deeper than a regular cream, and it carries the last two plants down with it. Pokeweed and white cedar break the wart down from the root, so there's nothing left to grow back.

lines.text: Any one of them alone stops halfway. Together, they reach the root.
And deep doesn't mean harsh. It's a kids' formula, for ages 4 and up.

lines.text: No acid, no freezing, no blister. Just a little cool tingle. And pediatricians recommend it.
At bedtime, it's three steps. File: rub the little file over it twice, just on the hard top. Soak: brush the oil on. Cover: a clear dot on top, so it soaks all night.
He's asleep before I put the cap back on.
Most spots, on a hand or a foot, are gone in about two weeks. Then you do fourteen more nights, so the root is gone too. Nobody gets held down, and there's nothing to book.
If your kid's wart keeps coming back, you've been stuck at number three. Skip to number four.
